# DraCuLa StreamNZB Template 6.4.4 — release notes draft

<!-- Auto-generated draft, seeded verbatim from the CHANGELOG section below. Condense for public release-note tone before merging the release-preparation PR -- this is a review starting point, not final prose. -->

## Changes

### Changed

- **formatter:** the production formatter's language line now shows `✓` instead of `⛿` when every displayed audio language was measured from the media file: `.LanguageSource` is `measured` and every `.Languages` entry is present in `.Probed.AudioLanguages`. `.LanguageSource` alone is not enough because `.Languages` merges measured, indexer-reported and name-inferred codes, so it can be `measured` while a displayed language was never confirmed. `✓` is expected on probed Library results; fresh indexer results keep `⛿`. The subtitle-only line, `.Subbed`/`.Subtitles` handling, subtitle flags and the 3+N overflow are unchanged, and so is the debug formatter. **Formatter refresh required**; no profile, Define, scoring or filtering change.
- **testing:** real-engine coverage through StreamNZB's own `newFormatContext` with real probe data (fully measured, partially measured, reported, inferred, untagged-probe fallback, subtitle-only, no metadata, measured with subtitle overflow). Each case also proves the output differs from the previous formatter only by `✓` versus `⛿`. Three production fixtures in `tests/streamnzb_compat/fixtures/formatter.json` cover the same marker.

### Fixed

- **scoring:** Anime BluRay tiers now score valid BluRay/BD-sourced remux releases. Jhin gives a remux the `remux` trait but never `bluray`, so the 16 `Anime Shows/Movies BluRay T1`-`T8` rules (`"bluray" in traits and not ("remux" in traits)`) never matched a remux: a `1080p.BluRay.REMUX-ZR` release scored exactly like an unknown-group remux (no `+400` BluRay T3), while Vidhin's `Anime BD T3` accepts it. The formatter itself was not broken; it only renders tiers that matched. Now that the rule matches, `.MatchedRules` carries `Anime Shows BluRay T3` and the existing production formatter shows `ʙʟᴜʀᴀʏ ᴛ₃` with no formatter change. The fix is in the generated classification, not in duplicated profile regexes. `scripts/sync_vidhin.py` has a new `anime_bd` mode, used by the 16 Anime BluRay targets in `scripts/vidhin_mapping.json`, that keeps three parts of upstream Vidhin's Anime BD records that standard-mode token extraction used to drop. (1) The outer physical-media source gate, translated to RE2 by rewriting its two lookaround forms. (2) Each record's own case flag: T3-T8 and the main T1/T2 records are case-insensitive; T1's `sam` record is case-sensitive, and T2's case-sensitive `[Orphan]` record adds nothing beyond the case-insensitive `-Orphan` token. (3) The T3 conditional branches: `PMR` only with a standalone `Remux` word, `NAN0` only after `remux`, and the mid-name `-ZR-` form. Group positions keep the existing end-anchored token model. The tier rules become `("bluray" in traits or "remux" in traits) and matched("... BluRay Tn Groups")`.
- **scoring:** remove the `group matches "(?i)^(LazyRemux|UltraRemux)$"` bypass from the 16 Anime BluRay tier rules. It predates source gating and accepted those two groups with no BD evidence: `1080p-LazyRemux` and `1080p.WEB-DL-LazyRemux` scored BluRay T4 (`+320`), and the UltraRemux equivalents scored T5 (`+240`), although upstream gives them no BD tier. BluRay-sourced LazyRemux/UltraRemux releases keep T4/T5 through the source-gated Defines.
- **scoring:** before → after (Anime Show and Anime Movie, real engine; parity with the live upstream regexes checked on 30 representative titles, 0 mismatches). Now scored: `BluRay`/`BD`/`BDMux`/`DVD`/`NTSC` `REMUX-ZR` (T3 `+400`), `BluRay.REMUX-PMR` and `BluRay.REMUX-NAN0` (T3), `BluRay.REMUX-ZR-v2` (T3; Jhin parses no group here), and `BluRay.REMUX-sam` (T1 `+560`). Each tiered remux beats the same remux from an untiered group by exactly its tier value. Still unscored: bare `REMUX-ZR`, `WEB-DL.REMUX-ZR`, `WEBRip.REMUX-ZR`, `BDRemux-PMR`, and lowercase `bluray.remux-sam`. No longer scored, matching upstream: bare and WEB-DL `LazyRemux`/`UltraRemux`; non-remux `BluRay.x265-PMR`/`-NAN0` (previously T3 because PMR/NAN0 were flattened into plain tokens); case-sensitive T1 `sam` spellings (`bluray.x264-sam`, `BluRay.x264-SAM`); and a dot-separated `Blu.Ray` encode (Jhin gives it the `bluray` trait, but upstream's gate only knows `BluRay`/`Blu-Ray`). Ordinary `BluRay` encodes are unchanged.
- **filtering:** `Reject bad 4K Anime` and `Trusted Release Groups` reference the same Anime BluRay Defines, so they now follow the source gate too. A 2160p WEB-DL from a group that is only in the Anime BD tiers (not in any Anime WEB tier) no longer counts as trusted 4K presence. In a pool with no other trusted 2160p candidate, it and the other untrusted 2160p candidates are now rejected, exactly like an unclassified 4K WEB (real-engine-confirmed; a 2160p BluRay from the same group still exempts the pool). Groups that are also in an Anime WEB tier are unaffected. `Anime Unknown Resolution`'s trusted exemption narrows the same way, for releases with no resolution, no parsed quality and no BD source token.
- **compatibility:** no rule or Define count change: 160/159 rules and 62 Defines. Group-token membership of every Define is identical; only the 16 Anime BluRay Define conditions and the 16 Anime BluRay rule conditions changed. Users must refresh both the Define Library and their profile (Define Library first). No 1080p-vs-4K ranking-policy change, no tier value change, no formatter change, no StreamNZB/Jhin pin change.
- **sync safety:** `validate_anime_bd_source()` makes the Vidhin sync fail closed if upstream changes the shared Anime BD source gate, any tier's per-record case flags, or the PMR/NAN0/`-ZR-` conditional branches, or if it adds a new lookaround/remux-conditional branch. This keeps the generated Defines from silently falling back to flattened token-only matching.
- **testing:** new `tests/streamnzb_compat/anime_bd_remux_tier_test.go` runs the published profile and generated Define library through the pinned engine. It covers every before/after case above for both Anime kinds, the exact tier-value delta against an untiered remux, and the `Reject bad 4K Anime` consequence, and it checks that the new production formatter fixture's `MatchedRules` (`Anime BluRay T3 remark on ZR remux`, `tests/streamnzb_compat/fixtures/formatter.json`) are exactly what the engine produces for that title. `TestAdjacentTierCeilingMatrix` gains `Anime Show BluRay REMUX` and `Anime Movie BluRay REMUX` families: adjacent-tier margins are identical to the encode families (−19 decorated vs clean, +18 vs RETAG'd), and native remux `+1500` only shifts the whole family. `tests/test_vidhin_sync.py` covers the `anime_bd` model (unchanged token membership, per-record case flags, conditional rendering, RE2-vs-upstream gate equivalence on 21 edge titles) and 7 drift scenarios. `tests/test_profile_defines.py` pins the exact tier-rule condition and requires the source gate and PMR/NAN0 conditions in the published Defines.
